content: Nicotine gum is prescribed to assist individuals in quitting smoking by serving as a substitute for the oral activity of smoking and providing a controlled source of nicotine to alleviate withdrawal symptoms associated with smoking cessation. Nicotine gum is intended for oral use and should not be swallowed. Follow the instructions on the product label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the gum exactly as directed, without exceeding or reducing the recommended dosage unless instructed by your doctor. Typically, treatment begins with the 2-mg gum. However, individuals who smoke more than 25 cigarettes per day may start with the 4-mg gum. The gum can be used regularly by chewing one piece every 1-2 hours initially, or it can be used as needed when the urge to smoke arises. To use nicotine gum properly, chew it slowly until you detect a nicotine taste or experience a mild tingling sensation in your mouth. At that point, stop chewing and park the gum between your cheek and gum. When the tingling subsides (usually after about one minute), resume chewing. Repeat this process for approximately 30 minutes. Avoid chewing the gum too quickly, using more than one piece at a time, or chewing pieces in rapid succession. If using the 2-mg gum, do not exceed 30 pieces per day under medical supervision or 24 pieces per day without supervision. For the 4-mg gum, do not exceed 24 pieces per day. After 2-3 months of use, gradually reduce the amount of nicotine gum to prevent withdrawal symptoms. Strategies for tapering off include: Reducing the total number of pieces used daily by one piece every 4-7 days. Decreasing the chewing time for each piece from 30 minutes to 10-15 minutes over 4-7 days, then gradually reducing the number of pieces used daily. Replacing one or more pieces of nicotine gum with sugarless gum, increasing the substitution every 4-7 days. Transitioning from 4-mg gum to 2-mg gum and applying the above steps. Discontinuing nicotine gum use when cravings are satisfied with one or two pieces per day. Prolonged use of nicotine gum beyond three months is not recommended, and use beyond six months should only occur under medical guidance. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, consult your doctor before using nicotine gum. If you become pregnant while using it, stop immediately and contact your doctor, as nicotine and nicotine gum can harm the fetus. Do not smoke or use other nicotine products while using nicotine gum to avoid nicotine overdose. Avoid eating or drinking, particularly acidic beverages like coffee or soft drinks, for 15 minutes before and during the use of nicotine gum, as this can interfere with nicotine absorption. Nicotine gum may cause mild side effects, including mouth ulcers, jaw muscle aches, dizziness, headache, and upset stomach. Notify your doctor if these symptoms persist or worsen. Severe side effects, such as seizures, heart rhythm disturbances, or difficulty breathing, require immediate medical attention. Serious side effects should be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store nicotine gum in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused gum properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all medical appointments while using nicotine gum. Do not share this medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Nicotine gum is available under brand names such as Nicorette® and Nicorette® DS, and it is also known as nicotine polacrilex.
